industry.why: Neutral at industry level, carried, with the sector rows carrying the view. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): technology saw $5.5 billion of net selling in the week, the most since January 2025 (Jefferies, 17 Oct), the rotation came out of it, and Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made'; against that, Jefferies finds sector pockets still upgrading inside it (analogue chips, optical networking, artificial-intelligence memory) and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: B now, B prior at industry level, carried by Semiconductors at A. The industry row stays C because the industry is split: Semiconductors (D), Software B2B Enterprise (D), Fintech (D) and Games (D) carry the Underweight; IT services, Hardware and vertical software stay Neutral. Counter-case for D: the heaviest net selling in 21 months is a regime statement; for B: the only industry with upgrades inside the sell-off.

sector.why: Underweight, carried unchanged, with the sector now split by the sources. Component 1 regime, 23-Oct-26 (risk-off confirmed and broadening: the discount-rate squeeze now a positioning wash-out in the artificial intelligence complex with credit leading it, bonds rallied as a hedge for the first time this cycle while the Fed still hikes in December, the US 10-year near 5.10%, Brent $111, French sovereign stress spilling into Italy, European defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows and breadth in the bottom fifth of three years; sources present 2026-W43): artificial-intelligence-linked semiconductors fell eight straight sessions to 16 Oct, technology net selling was the heaviest since January 2025, Wood says 'the easy money in semis is made', Korea fell about 20% in October on de-grossing, and the AI credits that set this row (the neoclouds) are 'the epicentre of the funding cost debate' (Goldman, 19 Oct); against it, Jefferies (22 Oct) is 'incrementally positive' on analogue chips with a read-across to Infineon and STMicroelectronics, sees China's equipment imports up 26% as the upside for 2027-28, and Morgan Stanley still rates North American semiconductors Attractive, while on equipment Jefferies' own headline is 'ASML - Still not excited'. Neither condition for C is met (no stabilisation read on the AI credits; no sell-side buy call on the European sector). Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-23 against 2026-08-21, not week on week: A now, A prior, the disagreement stated: the market still ranks the sector first while cutting its multiple. Ten of the 149 Pool stocks. Counter-case: the analogue upcycle 'has more legs' into 2027, demand was never the problem, and a D on ten Pool names pushes the Lists away from the one European industry with upgrades; the analogue read is a reason to look at STMicroelectronics stock by stock, not to move a row that is mostly equipment.

memo.verdict: Progress to Early-Stage Assessment, low conviction, with an explicit park trigger attached. The memo grades the memo-level Decision [C] and states the progression is conditional: the Early-Stage Assessment must run Element E3 (Sufficient total-shareholder-return / valuation upside) first, not last, and if Element E3 shows the remaining upside is inadequate at the prevailing price, the case parks at Early-Stage Assessment and does not proceed to Deep Dive. The memo states that progression authorises one more stage of analytical work, not capital, and that nothing in the memo supports a position at the current price. The recommendation is made against the on-disk risks report's Park stance, which the memo quotes and adopts in substance while overriding it only on the stage-gate question. The reasoning for progressing rather than parking is that the Triaging stage test is whether the case carries large amounts of positive change forces, and it plainly does; the valuation and entry-point question that would decide against the case is formally adjudicated at Element E3, which is first assessed at Early-Stage Assessment. The memo names an explicit park trigger so that the deferral is not open-ended.
case: The case for progressing rests on the magnitude, breadth and delivery of the change forces, which the memo grades Element E1 RA1 [A], the clearest [A] in the memo.

External change. The advanced substrate market moved from a nine-quarter overcapacity down-cycle into acute shortage, and pricing power has transferred to fabricators. Morgan Stanley estimates global advanced substrate pricing rising 20% to 25% in calendar 2026 and 25% or more through calendar 2027; Deutsche Bank's Brown raised his 2026 pricing forecast to an increase of 20% to 30% by year-end, from a prior 15% to 20%. Bernstein puts industry supply growth at a 12% compound rate against 22% demand growth through 2028. The physical driver is architectural rather than cyclical: modern multi-chiplet server processors require four times the net surface area and eight times the substrate capacity of pre-2023 designs. The integrated circuit package substrate market was USD 14.9bn in 2025 and is projected at USD 25.0bn by 2030, a 10.9% compound rate. Personal computers fall from 70% of substrate market value in 2015 to below 10% by 2030, while servers, accelerators, custom chips and networking exceed 80%.

Internal change. Element E8 RA3 grades [A] because seven of nine corporate-change deltas fired inside eighteen months. Guidance was increased twice, from 30% to 35% revenue growth and 25% to 29% margins, up to 45% to 55% and 32% to 37%. Balance sheet utilisation increased through the EUR 400m hybrid convertible at a 2.5% coupon and more than EUR 0.8bn of customer prepayments. The perimeter was reduced: the Ansan plant in Korea was sold for EUR 405m gross and EUR 353.4m net cash, booking a EUR 324.83m gain, Korea became a sales office, and the management board was cut from five to three. Strategy changed, with an explicit pivot from commoditised printed circuit boards to high-value computing and artificial-intelligence substrates under a stated zero-net-exposure investment model. Standards improved: earnings before interest and tax, and operating free cash flow, became the top internal performance metrics, and the short-term incentive was rebuilt to 40% earnings margin, 20% revenue and 20% free operating cash flow, against a prior structure weighted 80% to EBITDA alone. The actor set changed almost completely, and the chief executive changed. The two deltas that did not fire are shareholder returns, deliberately suspended to fund the capital programme, and mergers and acquisitions.
counter_case: The memo carries the counter-case at full force and grades it into the ratings rather than narrating it away.

The risks report recommends parking, and the memo quotes it. The on-disk risks report states that "the researcher recommends to Park the investment decision and wait for clear stabilization signs", rates confidence in the bear thesis being materially correct at medium plausibility, and records that "the probability of avoiding all failure states is low due to high balance sheet leverage" and that "the forward EPS trajectory possesses low operational resilience to exchange rate volatility". Its competing-hypotheses matrix names FALSE FRIEND the winner with one hard inconsistency against eleven for the bull profile and three for the bear.
triggers: Key questions carried to Early-Stage Assessment:
- How much of the change-from-current remains after a move from EUR 18.32 to EUR 148.2? The memo names this the question that decides the case.
- Does operating cash conversion recover in Q2, or is the Q1 divergence between EBITDA and cash the start of a trend?
- Does customer concentration fall as AMD ramps, or does the ramp simply replace one dependency with another?
- What is the economic, not reported, leverage path through the January 2027 hybrid call, and what happens if it is not called?
- How much of the 32% to 37% guided EBITDA margin survives the roll-off of one-time customer payments, and on what timetable?
